items.title: The problem with telling people the world is ending
items.description: <p>In the face of terrible crises, it can feel right to shock people into action. But what if that has the opposite effect?</p><p>These days, it’s easy to succumb to hopelessness. items.title: European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank
items.description: The Israeli military condemns the violence but the prime minister's office says it is part of a "smear" campaign.

items.title: Vietnam signs free trade deal with four European countries
items.description: Vietnam has signed a deal with four non-EU members that covers trade in goods and services, intellectual property rights, and sustainable development, among other areas.

sections.title: Beyond Climate & EU — World News Highlights

items.title: 'No Kings' rallies push early voting ahead of US midterm elections
items.description: Organizers of the "No Kings" protests, known for their anti-Trump sentiment, are urging Americans to vote early in the November 3 midterm elections, as Republicans face tough races to retain control of Congress.

items.title: Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting
items.description: About 1,800 people were arrested after nationwide protests saw outbreaks of violence and vandalism.

items.title: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
items.description: At least one person was killed in the strikes, which also hit a data centre used by Russia's equivalent of Facebook.

items.title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis
items.description: BBC News hears from users, dealers, prison and recovery workers as the country battles with a deadly new drug epidemic.

items.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
items.description: The US president temporarily ends many restrictions on Moscow recently passed by Congress over "national security" concerns.
